items.title: OpenAI shipped its cyber model on AWS
items.oneliner: OpenAI says GPT-5.6-Cyber found 400-plus privilege escalations. Offensive AI is now a cloud product, not a lab demo.

items.title: Qwen 3.8 made local multimodal serious
items.oneliner: Alibaba's Qwen 3.8 27B brings strong vision and coding to consumer hardware, but default reasoning still wastes latency.

items.title: OpenAI's best vision model just landed
items.oneliner: GPT-5.6 Sol jumped from 13.8 to 46.2 mAP@50 on counting-heavy vision tasks. Multimodal finally looks production-ready.

items.title: DeepSeek raised prices hard
items.oneliner: DeepSeek hiked V4-Pro cache-hit pricing by up to 1,114%. Cheap frontier inference is getting repriced in real time.

items.title: Claude watermarking became a product risk
items.oneliner: Anthropic's detectable text watermarking could expose AI-assisted writing at work or school. Compliance now changes output semantics.

items.title: ChatGPT on Mac raised logging alarms
items.oneliner: OpenAI's Mac computer-use feature reportedly logs keystrokes unencrypted. Agentic desktop control just hit a serious privacy wall.

items.title: AI scrapers are spoofing referral legitimacy
items.oneliner: AI scrapers now append fake tracking tags to look like legitimate traffic. Analytics pipelines are becoming attack surfaces.

items.title: Chainguard published osquery detections for production
items.oneliner: Chainguard released 250-plus osquery detection queries that stay silent until something breaks. That is how usable security tooling scales.

items.title: Protobuf finally got real editor support
items.oneliner: Buf shipped a production Protobuf LSP with completion and go-to-definition. Schema work just became much less painful.

items.title: A resale market formed for AI credits
items.oneliner: Token brokers are flipping unused AI credits at 30% to 80% discounts. Inference spend now has a gray market.
